profile.campus: Council Bluffs, Pottawattamie County, Iowa (CyrusOne OCB1)
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own facility page, OCB1 sits at 4700 Gifford Rd, Council Bluffs, IA 51501, publishing 9 MW of total IT capacity; CyrusOne's materials describe the site's technical IT space as roughly 420,000 sq ft total, of which about 120,000 sq ft is raised-floor white space, alongside a separately cited 216,000 sq ft total-footprint figure, three related-but-distinct figures noted here rather than collapsed into one. Per CyrusOne's own October 2023 blog post, OCB1 became the company's second North American data center (after DFW3 in Allen, Texas) to run on 100% renewable electricity, sourced via a green-tariff arrangement under MidAmerican Energy's GreenAdvantage program combining wind and solar projects; CyrusOne describes the arrangement as additional, regional, and bundled with renewable energy certificates, and frames it as supporting a company-wide climate-neutral-by-2030 goal (all of CyrusOne's European data centers were already on 100% renewable power at the time of that post). The Omaha-Council Bluffs market has drawn other large-scale data center investment (Google and Meta both operate major campuses in the area) partly due to Iowa's wind-generation capacity and MidAmerican Energy's renewable portfolio.

CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, was purchased by Cincinnati Bell for $525 million in 2010, completed an IPO in January 2013, and was taken private again when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) closed a roughly $15 billion acquisition on March 25, 2022.

The Omaha-Council Bluffs area's broader data center growth has drawn scrutiny in Iowa press over agricultural water use versus industrial power demand, a tension examined in outlets including Inside Climate News, which reported in 2025 on how federal clean-energy tax-credit policy changes could affect the economics that drew data center operators to Iowa's wind-heavy grid in the first place; CyrusOne's own framing of its renewable-energy deal as "additional," meaning the specific wind and solar projects would not have been built without this contract, distinguishes it from data center operators that simply purchase unbundled renewable energy certificates without funding new generation capacity.

sources.title: Harnessing the Wind and Sun: Council Bluffs Data Center Now Powered by 100% Renewable Electricity

reading.body:
OCB1 in Council Bluffs is rated for 9 MW of IT load, making it the largest published data center capacity in Iowa by the figures available here. The campus comprises 420,000 square feet of technical space, of which 120,000 square feet is raised floor and white space. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 9 MW of IT load would accommodate roughly 225 racks, though the operator has not published either a rack count or a breakdown of power allocation between storage, networking, and compute.

The facility holds certifications for PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, TIA-942, and HITRUST, qualifying it to host regulated workloads in healthcare, federal, and payment processing. These designations reflect compliance infrastructure rather than specialization for any particular tenant class. No information is published about current tenants, utilization, or committed capacity.

Iowa publishes 18 MW of total data center capacity across two facilities that disclose figures, with 52 mapped facilities overall. OCB1 accounts for half the state's published capacity, placing Iowa in the lower tier of US states for data center power. No opening date, recent investment, or power purchase arrangement for this campus is published.
